description: Hand-labeled expected clauses and risk flags for the sample contracts in data/sample_contracts. Used by tests/eval/run_eval.py to score the pipeline's clause recall and risk-flag precision against a known-correct answer.

documents.notes: All expected clauses are present in the source PDF text. liability_cap is expected to be flagged high risk because the cap (12 months of fees) is at the low end of what the risk taxonomy considers adequate.

This NDA intentionally has only a 1-year confidentiality survival period (short, per risk_taxonomy.csv 'Short Confidentiality Survival') and a Delaware governing-law clause (foreign jurisdiction relative to the other sample contracts). It has no termination-for-convenience clause and no liability cap clause at all, both flagged as missing by design.

Pairs with conflict_pair_b_long_notice.pdf (same counterparty: Vendor Company A / Vendor Company B) with a 30-day termination notice period vs the other document's 90-day period, feeding section 6's cross-portfolio conflict detection.
Pairs with conflict_pair_a_short_notice.pdf, 90-day termination notice vs the other document's 30-day notice.

The same confidentiality clause appears near-verbatim in section 1 and section 4 ('Confidentiality (Restated)'). Tests section 2's content_hash-based dedup: re-ingesting this document should upsert rather than create two separate confidentiality clause rows with identical normalized content.

Governing law is set to the Cayman Islands, an unexpected jurisdiction relative to an org profile whose jurisdiction_defaults.governing_law_country is 'IN' (both seeded org profiles default to IN). Should be flagged 'Unfavorable Governing Law' per risk_taxonomy.csv.

The liability cap clause uses vague non-standard wording ('a reasonable amount having regard to the circumstances') instead of a clean numeric cap, which should be flagged as high risk (no enforceable cap) and/or 'Non-Standard Wording' per risk_taxonomy.csv. Also expected to score a low org-profile deviation_score (section 4) against the approved liability_cap language, since there is no comparable numeric cap to align on.

Low-DPI (100 DPI) rendered image with no embedded PDF text layer at all (0 chars extracted by pdfplumber). Must go through detect_low_text_pages -> ocr_pages -> merge_ocr_results to recover any clause text. requires_ocr is false here because this repo's local eval environment doesn't have poppler/tesseract on PATH; the Docker image (see Dockerfile) installs both, so set this to true when running the eval inside that container to genuinely exercise OCR recovery. With OCR skipped, 0 clauses found here is expected/correct behavior for that code path, not a scoring failure.

Schedule A is a ReportLab platypus Table (9 rows x 5 columns: item code, description, unit price, minimum order quantity, lead time) on page 2, rendered with real grid lines so pdfplumber's extract_tables() should recover it as one table, not flatten it into clause text.
